items.check: Every code_change diff in the plan applies cleanly against the real tree at C:/codex/traktor-nml-tool: every context line is byte-identical to the current file content (no paraphrase, no re-wrapping, no altered whitespace/padding), every hunk header's -old,+new counts equal the actual number of context+removed and context+added lines in that hunk body, and every stated start line is within a few lines of where the context actually occurs. Verify by reconstructing each file and attempting the apply, not by eyeballing.

CC-M-003-004's doc_diff header '@@ -53,6 +53,49 @@' is correct: the DL-023 context lines it cites ('rewrite-from-collection-compare declaring new_input is the case / that motivated stating this generally (DL-023).') actually live at traktor_nml/README.md lines 99-101, not 53, and the hunk body adds 16 multi-line bullets (roughly 80 lines), not 43. Confirm the header start line and counts match reality.

Each of these hunk headers states an old-line count one greater than the number of context+removed lines actually present in its body (CC-M-002-001 '@@ -191,3', CC-M-002-002 '@@ -107,6' and '@@ -140,11', CC-M-003-001 '@@ -19,6', CC-M-003-003 '@@ -25,6'), and several start lines are off by one against the real files (playlists.py's 'return result' is at line 192 not 193; 'for node in find_playlist_nodes' is at 141 not 140; CLAUDE.md's spans.py row is at 19 with only 5 context lines shown).

DL-033 states the output-path refusal is done 'via rewrite.write_nml_safely's existing extra_inputs mechanism, not a bespoke check', but write_nml_safely is the attribute-patching (textpatch) write skeleton that DL-007 forbids mixing with the byte-span assembly path build-playlist uses, and no span-assembly command (splice_cmd, split_cmd) calls it. CC-M-002-006 correctly implements a bespoke set-membership check instead, yet its inline comment says 'mirroring splice_cmd.py's own bespoke tuple-membership check ... (DL-033)' - citing a decision that says the opposite of what the code and comment do. Verify the decision, the M-002 requirement, the acceptance criterion and the README bullet are all corrected to state the bespoke check that splice_cmd.py actually establishes.

The DL-033 bullet destined for traktor_nml/README.md's durable Design Decisions log does not assert the extra_inputs mechanism, which would leave a permanently false claim in the package's own log and invite a maintainer to 'fix' the working bespoke check by routing a span-assembly command through the textpatch write skeleton.

The test named as the sole verification of C-008 (build and validate wholly in memory; an abort leaves the output path untouched) can actually fail. As written it constructs output_path = tmp_path/'should_not_exist.nml', never passes it to assemble_output (which takes no output-path parameter at all), and then asserts it does not exist - an assertion that is true by construction and cannot detect a regression. Acceptance criterion 'Calling assemble_output directly on an input that produces an unresolved-tracks or no_entries_resolved error never creates, truncates, or otherwise touches the intended output path' therefore has no executable guard.

The M-002 test helper emits '<NODE TYPE="$ROOT" NAME="$ROOT">' as the PLAYLISTS root, but every real collection in testing/collections/ uses '<NODE TYPE="FOLDER" NAME="$ROOT">', and the existing suite's own helpers (tests/test_splice.py::_nml, tests/test_split.py::_nml) already use TYPE="FOLDER". Every target-folder test therefore exercises _find_target_subnodes' findall(".//NODE[@TYPE='FOLDER']") against a document whose root folder is invisible to that selector, which is not the production shape.

tracklist_bytes.decode("utf-8") is unguarded. A track list saved by a Windows editor in cp1252, or any non-UTF-8 encoding, raises UnicodeDecodeError that escapes the handler as a traceback instead of a diagnostic line plus exit 2, unlike every other input-error path in the package (input_not_found, xml_parse_error). A UTF-8 BOM is a second, quieter case: '\ufeffArtist' parses as an artist name that matches nothing, so the first line of every BOM-prefixed track list silently becomes an unresolved row.

The --unresolved-report path is excluded from the output-path refusal check, and the report is written even on an aborted run. An operator who points --unresolved-report at the base collection destroys it with CSV via a plain truncating open("w") - on a run the plan describes as writing nothing. Confirm whether extending the refusal set to the report path (and to splice_cmd's --conflict-report, which carries the same gap) is in scope or is a stated, accepted inheritance.

The target-folder lookup searches base_root.findall(".//NODE[@TYPE='FOLDER']") over the whole document rather than only the PLAYLISTS subtree, so a FOLDER node living outside PLAYLISTS could satisfy or falsely ambiguate the lookup. Confirm the search is scoped to the PLAYLISTS tree, matching DL-030's own wording ('more than one FOLDER anywhere in the PLAYLISTS tree').

The ambiguity error is returned as the string f"target_folder_ambiguous count={n}", which prints as one stderr line mixing a bare token and a key=value pair. Every other diagnostic in the package is either a bare token (no_root_subnodes, splice_aborted=true) or a single key=value (input_not_found=path). Confirm the spelling matches the package's one-diagnostic-per-line convention and that a test asserts on the token, not only on the exit code.

The valid-key validation 'if not set(matched_keys) <= valid_keys' compares keys taken from matched collection EntryRecords against the primary keys of those same records, so it is unfalsifiable and the invalid_primary_key branch is unreachable. R-010's stated mitigation ('every synthesized key is validated against the base collection's own primary keys') therefore mitigates nothing. Confirm whether the risk is real (and needs a check that can fire) or should be withdrawn along with the dead branch.

CI-M-003-004 says the new bullets go 'directly after the section's current final entry (DL-023)' and the acceptance criterion repeats 'immediately following its pre-existing DL-023 entry'. DL-023's bullet is at traktor_nml/README.md lines 97-101, and the Design Decisions section continues to line 140 - DL-023 is not the section's final entry. Confirm the intended insertion point and that the criterion states it accurately.

CC-M-002-005 creates commands/build_playlist_cmd.py whose register() binds handlers["build-playlist"] = _handle_build_playlist, a name only defined by CC-M-002-006, and imports assemble_output / read_and_parse_source / write_bytes_atomically / argparse that its own body never uses. Confirm the two changes are stated as one indivisible landing (the intermediate state raises NameError on any invocation and carries four unused imports).

The static-scope test checks only the forbidden-substring half of its stated contract. Acceptance criterion (C-007) and the test-list entry both also require 'matching.py and confidence.py remain byte-identical to their pre-existing contents', and M-001's acceptance criteria repeat it, but no test in either milestone asserts it. Confirm the byte-identity claim is either tested or restated as a review-time check.

match_records is called as match_records([record], collection, MatchConfidence.LOOSE, indexes=indexes) against the real signature match_records(old_records, new_records, confidence, key_providers=(), indexes=None). Confirm indexes is passed by keyword (it is, in the plan text) so key_providers is not accidentally bound positionally, and that passing new_records=collection alongside a prebuilt index does not trigger a second build_new_indexes pass (it does not - the build is guarded by 'if indexes is None').

mapping.get("") is a valid read-back for the matched record: match_records keys its mapping by old_record.primary_key, LocationParts.primary_key is volume+dir_value+file_name, and a tracklist_record's LocationParts is all-empty, so the key is exactly the empty string. Confirm no code path gives a tracklist record a non-empty location.

EntryRecord(entry=None, artist=..., title=..., audio_id="", filesize="", playtime_float="", bitrate="", album="", file_name="", location=LocationParts(volume="", volumeid="", dir_value="", file_name=""), source_path=None) names every field of the real dataclass with no missing or invented keyword, and the all-empty record survives match_records' own sample-collection path (record_label and location.decoded_path are both evaluated for a matched old record).

MatchConfidence.LOOSE genuinely admits the artist_title tier (confidence._LOOSE_TIERS = _STRICT_TIERS + ('artist_title',)) and no stricter tier is reachable for a record whose filesize, playtime_float, album, file_name and audio_id are all empty, so DL-032's 'every tier above artist_title is structurally unreachable' holds against the real record_keys guards.

The OutputBuilder call sequence matches spans.py's real API: add_verbatim(str), then add_counted_span(source, span, tag_name, count_attr, children, attr_patches=None, count=None) with count passed by keyword, then add_verbatim(str), then build(). Confirm the positional argument order and that count=existing_count+1 mirrors splice.py's own count=original_root_count+len(fragments) convention.

add_counted_span computes its insertion point as len(text) - len('</SUBNODES>'), which is wrong for a self-closing '<SUBNODES COUNT="0"/>' container - the fragment would be spliced inside the opening tag. No plan test covers that shape (the _nml helper always emits an explicit closing tag). Confirm whether a self-closing empty SUBNODES occurs in the real corpus, and if so whether this pre-existing spans.py limitation must be handled or documented for build-playlist's empty-root case.

playlists.py already imports uuid and ET at module level, so the new function's uuid.uuid4().hex and ET.Element/ET.SubElement/ET.tostring calls need no new import, and ET.tostring(node, encoding="unicode") returns str (matching the str-typed fragments OutputBuilder concatenates), not bytes.

The extraction is behavior-preserving: the removed inline block in import_playlists used original_name as the suffix base and mutated the caller's existing_names set, and available_playlist_name(requested_name, existing_names) reproduces both, including the in-place set mutation that splice.assemble_output relies on across contributions.

Every symbol buildplaylist.py imports exists at its stated source: collection_records in model.py; available_playlist_name (new), find_playlist_nodes and synthesize_playlist_node (new) in playlists.py; OutputBuilder, SpanIndex and find_element_span in spans.py; parse_tracklist and resolve_tracklist in tracklist.py. Confirm no import is left unused (SpanIndex and find_element_span are used only inside _find_target_subnodes, added in the second change).

The default branch's find_element_span(base_source, 'SUBNODES') takes the first SUBNODES in the document, exactly as splice.py:231 already does, while the named-folder branch resolves through SpanIndex(base_source, base_root).span_of(folder_subnodes). Confirm SpanIndex's ordinal-by-tag resolution is valid here (it requires the pre-order tree walk order to agree with source opening-tag order) and that a SpanIndex is not rebuilt per call in a loop.

existing_names is collected from find_playlist_nodes(base_root), which returns every NODE[@TYPE='PLAYLIST'] document-wide, so a name collision in a different folder from the insertion target still forces a '(2)' rename. Confirm this document-wide scope is intended (it matches splice.assemble_output:212) rather than a per-folder scope.

The skip test uses the stripped line ('not stripped or stripped.startswith("#")') while the delimiter search and both halves are taken from raw_line. Confirm this is deliberate and that a line whose only ' - ' occurrence sits inside leading whitespace (e.g. ' - Title') lands in the unparseable list via the empty-half guard, as the plan's own test asserts.

Both new test modules follow the suite's confirmed conventions: tests/test_build_playlist.py drives run_tool(argv, cwd) from tests.conftest for CLI-level guarantees (DL-011), and tests/test_tracklist.py's direct unit calls on pure parsing/resolution functions are a stated, justified exception rather than a silent departure from the CLI-level contract.

The test passes --allow-unmatched over a single-line all-unmatched tracklist and asserts exit_code == 2 because no_entries_resolved fires (DL-036) - so it exercises the zero-resolved abort, not the allow-unmatched CSV path it is named for. Confirm the CSV report assertion is still meaningful on that path, and that a separate case covers a report written alongside a successful partial build.

monkeypatch.setattr(build_playlist_cmd, 'write_bytes_atomically', _spy) actually intercepts the commit: the handler must reference the name through the module global (from ..rewrite import write_bytes_atomically, then a bare call), not via rewrite.write_bytes_atomically, for the patch to take effect. Confirm CC-M-002-006's import form matches what the test patches.

args.tracklist.read_bytes() catches only FileNotFoundError. A directory, an unreadable file, or a broken link raises IsADirectoryError/PermissionError/OSError that escapes as a traceback rather than the package's diagnostic-plus-exit-2 convention.

Every acceptance criterion in M-002 is backed by a listed test, and every listed test maps to a criterion. Specifically confirm coverage exists for 'The output document re-parses and every byte outside the receiving SUBNODES matches the base' and 'Each new PRIMARYKEY KEY equals the matched collection entry's primary key, not a value derived from the input text' - the CC-M-002-007 body asserts substring ordering and counts but no byte-level comparison against the base outside the receiving span.

Every decision_refs entry across all 13 code_intents (CI-M-001-001..003, CI-M-002-001..006, CI-M-003-001..004) names a decision that exists in planning_context.decisions (DL-024..DL-039), and every rejected_alternative's decision_ref (RA-001..RA-012) and every risk's decision_ref (R-006..R-011) likewise resolves. No new DL id collides with the pre-existing package log, whose maximum is DL-023.

Every code_intent has at least one code_change carrying its id in intent_ref, and every code_change either names a real intent_ref or is a test change with intent_ref null. Confirm CI-M-002-004 (BuildPlaylistResult) maps to CC-M-002-003 and CI-M-002-003 (assemble_output) to CC-M-002-004, which are cross-ordered relative to their ids.

No file listed in a milestone's files[] lacks a code_change, and no code_change touches a file absent from its milestone's files[]. Confirm traktor_nml/playlists.py appears in M-002's files (it does) and that no change silently edits matching.py or confidence.py, which C-001 forbids.
